name: gitlab-go-ci-gates
description: Recommends the team's blocking Go checks in GitLab CI without emitting GitHub Actions configuration
prompt: Set up CI for a Go service in our GitLab monorepo. What checks should the Go child pipeline run?
trap: The answer may generate GitHub Actions or miss module verification, race-enabled tests, lint, or govulncheck.

assertions.text: Uses GitLab CI and points to gitlab-ci for pipeline syntax and the shared Go template
Includes formatting, go vet, configured golangci-lint, and go test -race
Includes go mod tidy followed by a diff check of go.mod and go.sum
Recommends govulncheck and says to pin its version
Does not output GitHub Actions workflow configuration

name: integration-test-cache
description: Requires uncached real-service tests without confusing Go test-result and build caches
prompt: Our Go tests use PostgreSQL in GitLab CI. Sometimes the database was changed but Go reports cached tests. What should the test command do?
trap: The answer may disable the build cache or suggest hiding the integration tests behind a tag instead of disabling result caching.

assertions.text: Uses -count=1 for tests dependent on external service state
Explains that -count=1 disables test-result caching, not the Go build cache
Keeps real database tests in the normal test suite in line with go-testing
May recommend -shuffle=on to expose order-dependent tests

name: gitlab-go-service-release
description: Uses the team's GitLab service release path instead of GoReleaser or GitHub workflows by default
prompt: Add CI deployment for a Go HTTP service. Should I use GoReleaser and the upstream Docker GitHub Actions workflow?
trap: The answer may copy upstream GitHub Actions or conflate a Go service's image/chart release with publishing CLI binaries.

assertions.text: Says Go services use the GitLab image and chart-release templates in gitlab-ci
Does not use GoReleaser as the default service deployment path
Distinguishes standalone binary or library release use cases from service deployment
